Because the story is written entirely in a script/play format, it relies almost exclusively on exteriority—specifically dialogue and brief stage directions describing observable physical actions (e.g., turning a cup, keeping a jacket on, briefly smiling). While there is rich emotional subtext implied through the characters' words and behaviors, there is virtually no direct interiority, introspection, or explicit portrayal of the characters' inner thoughts and memories, apart from one brief omniscient note that Thomas looks at his watch "without having read the time." Therefore, it does not balance action and introspection, even though the exteriority effectively hints at deeper emotions.
